correctness.rationale: For each n=2m, the maximal operator output is independently selected among identity, (S-a_antipode)/(n-1), and S/n. The squared norm is maximum of eigenvalues over 3^n row-selection matrices. For every nonexceptional row choice, a positive integer vector v satisfies (V I-H^T H)v>0 entrywise, proving by Perron spectral comparison strict exclusion. The independently reconstructed full 66,420-choice script verified exactly 66,401 nonexceptional inequalities and the 19 exceptional pattern counts (2,3,4,10); minimum strict integer margin was positive in each m. Exceptional matrices reduce to a 2x2 constant-block spectral equation with top root above rational threshold and uniquely positive eigenvector; direct inequalities verify exactly selected averaging radii and all sign freedoms. No claim for m>5.
